rationale: KAPS remains an active Canadian pipeline system, but Stonepeak is no longer an owner. Stonepeak's 50% entry closed on April 26, 2023, and Keyera signed and closed the C$1.215 billion purchase of that remaining 50% on June 17, 2026, reaching 100% ownership. August 2026 results reconfirmed the completed acquisition and continuing operations, so only Stonepeak's ownership period should be retired.
recommendedChanges: Retain one canonical KAPS Pipeline company with Key Access Pipeline System as its expanded identity.
Retire Stonepeak's 50% ownership period effective June 17, 2026 and preserve its April 26, 2023 entry date.
Record Keyera as the active 100% owner from June 17, 2026 while preserving its original 50% ownership history from 2019.
Record Kentucky Middle Holdings, LP as seller and Kentucky MidCo, Ltd. as the acquired interest-holding entity; do not invent an undisclosed Keyera title affiliate.
Keep Zones 1 through 4 within the single KAPS system and keep connected Keyera processing, fractionation and storage assets outside the PortCo boundary.
Preserve KAPS as active; the transaction was an owner exit, not a company realization or shutdown.
unresolvedQuestions: Stonepeak's fund, Keyera's exact title-holding affiliate, the unnamed PGI seller subsidiary and the precise first-flow day are not publicly disclosed.
